caveats: Identity boundary: Kim Myong Chol is the person named in the MSMT Annex 7 KMCTC employment table. Giang, John, Julian, and Luan are source-reported employment labels only; they are not established civil identities, separate people, or evidence of present account control. The same name also appears for an OFAC-listed SEK Studio representative and in UN reporting on an Oh Chung Song-associated Dubai/Vientiane group; neither record is merged because no reviewed source provides a unique identity bridge to the KMCTC worker.
Employment aliases may be stolen, borrowed, or synthetic identities; do not imply that the apparent alias owner is the DPRK worker.

Identity-document imagery is do-not-publish evidence only. Do not export, cache, crop, transcribe, OCR, reproduce, perform facial recognition or identity matching, resolve aliases, or infer current appearance or location; preserve citation provenance only.

The source also lists single-name alias labels for this individual: Giang, John, Julian, Luan. They are kept out of the searchable name fields because a bare first name identifies nobody; see the sourced facts for their context.

No connection is asserted to Kim Myong-chol (born 1944), the Japan-based writer described as an unofficial DPRK spokesman, nor to the OFAC-designated SEK Studio representative of the same name. MSMT's identity table gives a birth date a decade apart from OFAC's.
Accounts and handles are historical observations reported by the cited sources. Present control of any account is not asserted, and a persona name is not asserted to be anyone's legal identity.
